newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Philippine economy grew by a respectable 6.1 percent growh in the first quarter despite a slowdown in the manufacturing sector, the National Statistical Coordinating Board says. (ALL PAPERS)
- Supreme Court chief Justice Andres Narvasa hits back at reporters who wrote about the alleged corruption in the judiciary, saying the allegations were unfounded and plain rumours (ALL PAPERS)

- The Philippine Coast Guard, brushing aside protests from Beijing, lodges with a criminal complaint against 21 Chinese fishernmen arrested near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea for illegal entry. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- United States ambassador Thomas Hubbard says the United States is not seeking a new base in the Philippines, noting that the Mutual Defense Treaty already provides for a US military presence in the Pacific (ALL PAPERS)
- The country's net oil import bill increases by 23.5 percent to $724 million in the first quarter of the year due to higher crude prices. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- The United States complaint against the Philippines' failure to comply with its pork and poultry market access commitments under the World Trade Organisatin will become a full-blown dispute by June or July, a Philippine official said. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Central Bank cuts most of its key interest rates as speculation in the foreign exchange market calmed down. (TODAY)

- The Philippine Stock Exchange may permanently ban the operations of the four stockbrokerage houses accused by newspaper columnist Ninez Cacho Olivares of defrauding her, PSE president Jose Yulo says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
